\end{longtable}
\endgroup

Every deterministic plan has all four correlators equal to $\pm 1$, so $p = 1 - 1 - 1 = -1$
and every one of the sixteen fails.

\begin{remark}[What PSD of the pinned matrix means]\label{rem:chsh-scope-five}
$M(E)$ is the level-1 moment matrix with the two within-party entries $\langle A_0 A_1
\rangle$ and $\langle B_0 B_1 \rangle$ pinned to zero. Its PSD is sufficient for the
correlators to admit some PSD completion (item G, \code{zero\_marginal\_implies\_elliptope}), and it
is not necessary: the all-ones plan has a completion but fails here. So a check built on
$M(E)$ is sound for the completion set and not complete for it, and it rejects some honest
classical tallies. That correlators with a PSD completion are exactly those reachable by
quantum measurements is Tsirelson's theorem, cited and not proved here (item H).
\end{remark}

\subsection{E. The integer check}
\label{sub:chsh-integer}

\begin{definition}[\code{column\_contractive\_check\_witness}]\label{def:chsh-check}
(kernel/foundation/VMStep.v) From the counters of Definition~\ref{def:chsh-counters}, with all
arithmetic in $\mathbb{Z}$, let
\[
\begin{aligned}
A &= N_{00}^2 N_{10}^2 - D_{00}^2 N_{10}^2 - D_{10}^2 N_{00}^2, \\
B &= N_{01}^2 N_{11}^2 - D_{01}^2 N_{11}^2 - D_{11}^2 N_{01}^2, \\
C &= D_{00} D_{01} N_{10} N_{11} + D_{10} D_{11} N_{00} N_{01}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The check is the conjunction of seven facts, in this order:
$0 < N_{00}$, $0 < N_{01}$, $0 < N_{10}$, $0 < N_{11}$, $0 \le A$, $0 \le B$, and
$C \cdot C \le A \cdot B$.
\end{definition}

There is no division, no real number, no square root and no $S$ in it.

\begin{lemma}[The seven facts are the three conditions with denominators cleared]\label{lem:chsh-clear}
Assume $N_{00}, N_{01}, N_{10}, N_{11} > 0$ and put $E_{xy} = D_{xy}/N_{xy}$. Then, with
$p, q, s$ as in Definition~\ref{def:chsh-cc},
\[
\begin{gathered}
p = \frac{A}{N_{00}^2 N_{10}^2}, \qquad q = \frac{B}{N_{01}^2 N_{11}^2}, \qquad
s = \frac{C}{N_{00} N_{01} N_{10} N_{11}}, \\
pq - s^2 = \frac{AB - C^2}{(N_{00} N_{01} N_{10} N_{11})^2}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Because every denominator is positive, $0 \le A \iff p \ge 0$, $0 \le B \iff q \ge 0$ and
$C^2 \le AB \iff s^2 \le pq$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For $p$: $1 - D_{00}^2/N_{00}^2 - D_{10}^2/N_{10}^2$; multiply by $N_{00}^2 N_{10}^2$ to get
$N_{00}^2 N_{10}^2 - D_{00}^2 N_{10}^2 - D_{10}^2 N_{00}^2 = A$. For $q$ the same with
columns $01$ and $11$, multiplied by $N_{01}^2 N_{11}^2$. For $s$:
\[
\frac{D_{00}}{N_{00}} \frac{D_{01}}{N_{01}} + \frac{D_{10}}{N_{10}} \frac{D_{11}}{N_{11}}
= \frac{D_{00} D_{01} N_{10} N_{11} + D_{10} D_{11} N_{00} N_{01}}{N_{00} N_{01} N_{10} N_{11}}
= \frac{C}{N_{00} N_{01} N_{10} N_{11}} .
\]
Then
$pq = AB / (N_{00}^2 N_{10}^2 N_{01}^2 N_{11}^2) = AB/(N_{00} N_{01} N_{10} N_{11})^2$ and
$s^2 = C^2/(N_{00} N_{01} N_{10} N_{11})^2$; subtract. Multiplying an inequality by a
positive number preserves it in both directions.
\end{proof}

The Coq source states the direction it needs:

\begin{theorem}[Soundness of the integer check]\label{thm:chsh-check-sound}
If \code{column\_contractive\_check\_witness} $w$ = \code{true}, then the four correlators
\code{state\_bucket\_correlation} $\mathrm{same}_{xy}\ \mathrm{diff}_{xy}$ of $w$ are column
contractive. This is \code{column\_contractive\_check\_witness\_sound}
(kernel/nfi/MuLedgerQuantumBridge.v), lifted to a machine state as
\code{state\_column\_contractive\_check\_witness\_sound}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first four conjuncts make every $N_{xy}$ positive, so the empty-bucket convention never
applies and each correlator is $D_{xy}/N_{xy}$. The integer facts lift to the reals by the
injection $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$, which preserves order. Lemma~\ref{lem:chsh-clear} turns them
into the three conditions.
\end{proof}

The instruction is defined by two step rules. \code{step\_chsh\_lassert\_ok}
(kernel/foundation/VMStep.v): when the check is true, the program counter advances by
one and every other field is unchanged except the cost counter. \code{step\_chsh\_lassert\_bad}: when it is false, the program counter goes to \code{LASSERT\_TRAP\_PC} $= 3840$,
the error flag is set, and the error register is set to 1. Both branches charge the declared
cost plus one (\textnormal{\texttt{S mu\_delta}}).

\begin{theorem}[No trap implies PSD, \code{chsh\_lassert\_no\_trap\_implies\_npa\_psd}]\label{thm:chsh-notrap}
(kernel/quantum/QuantumPartitionPSD.v) Let $s$ be a state with error flag false, and let
$s'$ be the result of applying \code{instr\_chsh\_lassert} $d$ to $s$, where $d$ is the declared cost. If the error flag of
$s'$ equals that of $s$, then
\code{npa\_psd} holds of \code{state\_zero\_marginal\_npa} $s$: the pinned matrix $M(E)$ built from the
correlators of $s$'s counters is symmetric and PSD.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If the check had failed, the step would set the error flag to true, contradicting ``error
flag unchanged and false before''. So the check passed. Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-check-sound} gives column
contractivity, and Corollary~\ref{cor:chsh-iff} gives PSD. The intermediate form is
\code{chsh\_lassert\_check\_implies\_npa\_psd} (QuantumPartitionPSD.v).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No trap implies the Tsirelson bound]\label{cor:chsh-notrap-bound}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-notrap}, the correlators of $s$'s counters satisfy
$S^2 \le 8$. There is no single named theorem for this; it is the composition of
Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-notrap} with Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-psd-tsirelson} (the matrix \code{state\_zero\_marginal\_npa}
$s$ unfolds to \code{zero\_marginal\_npa} of the four state correlators). The same conclusion is
also reached through \code{chsh\_lassert\_no\_trap\_implies\_state\_column\_contractive}
(kernel/nfi/MuLedgerQuantumBridge.v) and \code{state\_column\_contractive\_implies\_tsirelson}.
\end{corollary}

A worked tally. Take $(\mathrm{same}, \mathrm{diff}) = (4,1), (4,1), (4,1), (1,4)$ for the
pairs $00, 01, 10, 11$. Then $N_{xy} = 5$ for all four, $D_{00} = D_{01} = D_{10} = 3$,
$D_{11} = -3$, and the correlators are $0.6, 0.6, 0.6, -0.6$ with $S = 2.4$. Compute:
\[
\begin{aligned}
A &= 25 \cdot 25 - 9 \cdot 25 - 9 \cdot 25 = 625 - 225 - 225 = 175, \\
B &= 25 \cdot 25 - 9 \cdot 25 - 9 \cdot 25 = 175, \\
C &= 3 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 5 + 3 \cdot (-3) \cdot 5 \cdot 5 = 225 - 225 = 0 .
\end{aligned}
\]
All seven facts hold: four positive $N$, $0 \le 175$ twice, and $0 \le 175 \cdot 175$.
Dividing back, $p = 175/625 = 0.28$ and $s = 0$, the second row of the table in item D.

Two more, for contrast. One round per pair from the all-ones plan, $(1,0)$ four times, gives
$N = D = 1$ everywhere and $A = 1 - 1 - 1 = -1 < 0$: trap. The tally $(4,1), (9,1), (9,1),
(1,4)$ gives correlators $3/5, 4/5, 4/5, -3/5$, with $N = 5, 10, 10, 5$ and
$D = 3, 8, 8, -3$:
$A = 25 \cdot 100 - 9 \cdot 100 - 64 \cdot 25 = 0$,
$B = 100 \cdot 25 - 64 \cdot 25 - 9 \cdot 100 = 0$ and
$C = 3 \cdot 8 \cdot 10 \cdot 5 + 8 \cdot (-3) \cdot 5 \cdot 10 = 0$. It passes with no
slack, at $S = 2.8$.

\begin{remark}[The circuit]\label{rem:chsh-circuit}
The hardware check is proved equal to this definition. \code{chsh\_check\_nat\_correct}
(kami\_\allowbreak{}hw/ChshArith.v) equates a natural-number form with
\code{column\_contractive\_check\_witness}; \code{chsh\_check\_word\_correct} (ChshArith.v) and
\code{chsh\_check\_word\_spec} equate the word-level circuit with it for every choice of
eight 32-bit counters. The intermediate products are carried at 134 bits and the product
$A \cdot B$ at 268 bits (ChshArith.v). \code{chsh\_run\_result} (kami\_\allowbreak{}hw/ChshRun.v)
composes the 29 firings of the check, and \code{chsh\_lassert\_refines} (kami\_\allowbreak{}hw/ChshRetire.v)
is the refinement statement. Section~\ref{sec:chip} tells that part.
\end{remark}

\subsection{F. Level 1+AB}
\label{sub:chsh-q1ab}

The source indexes Alice's observables $A_1, A_2$ and Bob's $B_1, B_2$; I keep the book's
$A_0, A_1, B_0, B_1$, so the Coq $e_{11}$ is $E_{00}$ here, and so on. The five extra
parameters are named in the record \code{Q1ABMoments} (kernel/quantum/QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v):
$\gamma_1$ for $\langle A_0 A_1 B_0 \rangle$, $\gamma_2$ for $\langle A_0 A_1 B_1 \rangle$,
$\gamma_3$ for $\langle A_0 B_0 B_1 \rangle$, $\gamma_4$ for $\langle A_1 B_0 B_1 \rangle$,
$\gamma_5$ for $\langle A_0 A_1 B_0 B_1 \rangle$. These are labels only; the file builds no
operators.

\begin{definition}[\code{q1ab\_moment\_matrix}]\label{def:chsh-nine}
(kernel/quantum/QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v) The $9 \times 9$ real matrix on rows and
columns $I, A_0, A_1, B_0, B_1, A_0B_0, A_0B_1, A_1B_0, A_1B_1$, with the entries exactly as
the Coq definition places them:
\end{definition}

\[
\setlength{\arraycolsep}{3.2pt}
\begin{array}{c|ccccccccc}
 & I & A_0 & A_1 & B_0 & B_1 & A_0B_0 & A_0B_1 & A_1B_0 & A_1B_1 \\ \hline
I      & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & E_{00} & E_{01} & E_{10} & E_{11} \\
A_0    & 0 & 1 & 0 & E_{00} & E_{01} & 0 & 0 & \gamma_1 & \gamma_2 \\
A_1    & 0 & 0 & 1 & E_{10} & E_{11} & \gamma_1 & \gamma_2 & 0 & 0 \\
B_0    & 0 & E_{00} & E_{10} & 1 & 0 & 0 & \gamma_3 & 0 & \gamma_4 \\
B_1    & 0 & E_{01} & E_{11} & 0 & 1 & \gamma_3 & 0 & \gamma_4 & 0 \\
A_0B_0 & E_{00} & 0 & \gamma_1 & 0 & \gamma_3 & 1 & 0 & 0 & \gamma_5 \\
A_0B_1 & E_{01} & 0 & \gamma_2 & \gamma_3 & 0 & 0 & 1 & -\gamma_5 & 0 \\
A_1B_0 & E_{10} & \gamma_1 & 0 & 0 & \gamma_4 & 0 & -\gamma_5 & 1 & 0 \\
A_1B_1 & E_{11} & \gamma_2 & 0 & \gamma_4 & 0 & \gamma_5 & 0 & 0 & 1
\end{array}
\]

Two conventions are fixed by this layout. First, the four-body cells carry opposite signs:
$+\gamma_5$ at $(A_0B_0, A_1B_1)$ and $-\gamma_5$ at $(A_0B_1, A_1B_0)$. The file states this
is a convention of the real matrix, not derived from operators, and guards it with
\code{q1ab\_four\_body\_cells\_are\_conjugate} (QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v). Second, the matrix
keeps the level-1 pinning: every cell whose label reduces to a marginal or to
$\langle A_0 A_1 \rangle$ or $\langle B_0 B_1 \rangle$ is zero, for instance
$(A_0, A_0B_0)$, $(A_0B_0, A_0B_1)$ and $(A_0B_0, A_1B_0)$. Symmetry is
\code{q1ab\_moment\_matrix\_symmetric}.

Write a vector as $(v_I, v_{A_0}, v_{A_1}, v_{B_0}, v_{B_1}, v_{00}, v_{01}, v_{10}, v_{11})$,
where $v_{xy}$ is the coordinate of $A_xB_y$. Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
L_1 &= E_{00} v_{00} + E_{01} v_{01} + E_{10} v_{10} + E_{11} v_{11}, \\
L_2 &= E_{00} v_{B_0} + E_{01} v_{B_1} + \gamma_1 v_{10} + \gamma_2 v_{11}, \\
L_3 &= E_{10} v_{B_0} + E_{11} v_{B_1} + \gamma_1 v_{00} + \gamma_2 v_{01}.
\end{aligned}
\]

\begin{definition}[The residual, \code{q1ab\_residual}]\label{def:chsh-residual}
(QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v)
\[
\begin{aligned}
R ={}& v_{B_0}^2 + v_{B_1}^2 + v_{00}^2 + v_{01}^2 + v_{10}^2 + v_{11}^2 \\
&+ 2 v_{B_0} (\gamma_3 v_{01} + \gamma_4 v_{11}) + 2 v_{B_1} (\gamma_3 v_{00} + \gamma_4 v_{10}) \\
&+ 2 \gamma_5 (v_{00} v_{11} - v_{01} v_{10}) - L_1^2 - L_2^2 - L_3^2 .
\end{aligned}
\]
The predicate \code{column\_contractive\_q1ab} says $R \ge 0$ for all six real inputs.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Three squares plus the residual, \code{quad9\_q1ab\_sos\_decomposition}]\label{lem:chsh-nine-sos}
(QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v, closed by \code{ring}.) For every vector,
\[
v^{\mathsf T} M_9\, v = (v_I + L_1)^2 + (v_{A_0} + L_2)^2 + (v_{A_1} + L_3)^2 + R .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The coordinates $v_I$, $v_{A_0}$, $v_{A_1}$ appear in the form only through their diagonal
squares and the cross terms $2 v_I L_1$, $2 v_{A_0} L_2$, $2 v_{A_1} L_3$, read off rows
$I$, $A_0$, $A_1$ of the matrix. Completing each square adds $L_1^2 + L_2^2 + L_3^2$, which
the residual subtracts. What is left in $R$ is the diagonal of the remaining six coordinates
and the cross terms among them, read off the lower right $6 \times 6$ block.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[PSD at level 1+AB, \code{q1ab\_psd\_iff\_column\_contractive}]\label{thm:chsh-nine-iff}
(QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v) For all real $E_{xy}$ and $\gamma_1, \ldots, \gamma_5$,
\code{PSD9} of the matrix of Definition~\ref{def:chsh-nine} holds if and only if \code{column\_contractive\_q1ab}
holds. The directions are \code{column\_contractive\_q1ab\_implies\_psd9} and
\code{psd9\_implies\_column\_contractive\_q1ab}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $R \ge 0$ everywhere, Lemma~\ref{lem:chsh-nine-sos} writes the form as three squares plus $R$.
Conversely, given the six residual inputs, choose $v_I = -L_1$, $v_{A_0} = -L_2$,
$v_{A_1} = -L_3$; the three squares vanish and PSD gives $R \ge 0$. This is the level-1
argument of item D one size up.
\end{proof}

As a quadratic form in $(v_{B_0}, v_{B_1}, v_{00}, v_{01}, v_{10}, v_{11})$, numbered 1 to 6,
the residual has the symmetric coefficient matrix $H$ with these upper entries. They are the
\code{q12345\_H11} to \code{q12345\_H66} definitions (QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v onward), and
\code{q12345\_sym6\_qf\_equals\_residual} proves the form equals $R$. Each entry can be read
back off $R$ by collecting the coefficient of $v_i v_j$.

\begin{align*}
H_{11} &= 1 - E_{00}^2 - E_{10}^2, & H_{22} &= 1 - E_{01}^2 - E_{11}^2, \\
H_{12} &= -(E_{00}E_{01} + E_{10}E_{11}), & H_{13} &= -E_{10}\gamma_1, \\
H_{14} &= \gamma_3 - E_{10}\gamma_2, & H_{15} &= -E_{00}\gamma_1, \\
H_{16} &= \gamma_4 - E_{00}\gamma_2, & H_{23} &= \gamma_3 - E_{11}\gamma_1, \\
H_{24} &= -E_{11}\gamma_2, & H_{25} &= \gamma_4 - E_{01}\gamma_1, \\
H_{26} &= -E_{01}\gamma_2, & H_{33} &= 1 - E_{00}^2 - \gamma_1^2, \\
H_{34} &= -(E_{00}E_{01} + \gamma_1\gamma_2), & H_{35} &= -E_{00}E_{10}, \\
H_{36} &= \gamma_5 - E_{00}E_{11}, & H_{44} &= 1 - E_{01}^2 - \gamma_2^2, \\
H_{45} &= -\gamma_5 - E_{01}E_{10}, & H_{46} &= -E_{01}E_{11}, \\
H_{55} &= 1 - E_{10}^2 - \gamma_1^2, & H_{56} &= -(E_{10}E_{11} + \gamma_1\gamma_2), \\
H_{66} &= 1 - E_{11}^2 - \gamma_2^2 .
\end{align*}

The top left $2 \times 2$ block is $I_2 - E^{\mathsf T} E$ from item D.

The full check does not decide $R \ge 0$ directly. It proves the stronger fact that $H$ is
positive definite, by two Schur steps and a Sylvester test, all fraction-free.

\begin{lemma}[Fraction-free Schur step]\label{lem:chsh-schur-step}
For a symmetric $n \times n$ matrix $h$ and any vector $v$, with
$S_{ij} = h_{11} h_{ij} - h_{1i} h_{1j}$ for $i, j \ge 2$ (here $S$ is the Schur matrix, not
the score),
\[
h_{11} \, v^{\mathsf T} h\, v = \Bigl(\sum_{j} h_{1j} v_j\Bigr)^2 + \sum_{i,j \ge 2} S_{ij} v_i v_j .
\]
So if $h_{11} > 0$ and the $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ matrix $S$ gives a nonnegative form, then $h$
does too. The instances used are \code{sym6\_Schur\_identity} (QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v) and
\code{sym5\_Schur\_identity}, with the conclusions \code{sym6\_qf\_nonneg\_from\_pd} and
\code{sym5\_qf\_nonneg\_from\_pd}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Expand the square: $h_{11}^2 v_1^2 + 2 h_{11} v_1 \sum_{j \ge 2} h_{1j} v_j +
(\sum_{j \ge 2} h_{1j} v_j)^2$. The left side is
$h_{11}^2 v_1^2 + 2 h_{11} v_1 \sum_{j \ge 2} h_{1j} v_j + h_{11} \sum_{i,j \ge 2} h_{ij} v_i v_j$.
The difference is $\sum_{i,j \ge 2} (h_{11} h_{ij} - h_{1i} h_{1j}) v_i v_j$. Dividing by
$h_{11} > 0$ keeps the sign.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Sylvester for 4x4, \code{sym4\_qf\_nonneg\_from\_pd}]\label{lem:chsh-sylvester}
(QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v) Let $h$ be symmetric $4 \times 4$ with leading principal
minors $d_1, d_2, d_3, d_4$ (\code{sym4\_d1} to \code{sym4\_d4}). If all four are
strictly positive, then $v^{\mathsf T} h\, v \ge 0$ for all $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\code{sym4\_LDLT\_identity} (closed by \code{ring}) is the fraction-free factorization
\[
d_1^2 d_2 d_3 \, v^{\mathsf T} h\, v = d_1 d_2 d_3 \, P_1^2 + d_1 d_3 \, Q_1^2 + Q_2^2 +
d_1^2 d_2 d_4 \, v_4^2,
\]
where $P_1 = \sum_j h_{1j} v_j$, $Q_1 = (h_{11}h_{22} - h_{12}^2) v_2 + (h_{11}h_{23} -
h_{12}h_{13}) v_3 + (h_{11}h_{24} - h_{12}h_{14}) v_4$, and $Q_2$ is the third linear form
(\code{sym4\_Q2}). With every $d_k > 0$ the right side is nonnegative and the factor on the
left is positive.
\end{proof}

The cascade for the full check runs on $H$. Step one: $H_{11} > 0$ and the $5 \times 5$
matrix $S^{(6)}_{ij} = H_{11} H_{ij} - H_{1i} H_{1j}$, $2 \le i, j \le 6$, gives a nonnegative
form. Step two: $S^{(6)}_{22} > 0$ and the $4 \times 4$ matrix
$S^{(5)}_{ij} = S^{(6)}_{22} S^{(6)}_{ij} - S^{(6)}_{2i} S^{(6)}_{2j}$, $3 \le i, j \le 6$,
gives a nonnegative form. Step three: the four leading minors of $S^{(5)}$ are positive. The
real predicates are \code{sym5\_pd\_interior}, \code{sym6\_pd\_interior} and the witness
\code{q1ab\_g12345\_minors\_witness}, which implies \code{column\_contractive\_q1ab} and
then \code{PSD9} (\code{q1ab\_g12345\_minors\_witness\_implies\_psd9}).

\begin{definition}[What the integer check computes]\label{def:chsh-g12345}
The supplied moments arrive as bucket pairs: $\gamma_k = N_{g_k}/D_{g_k}$ with
$N_{g_k} = \mathrm{same}_{g_k} - \mathrm{diff}_{g_k}$ and
$D_{g_k} = \mathrm{same}_{g_k} + \mathrm{diff}_{g_k}$. Watch the letters: for these five
buckets the source swaps them, so here $N$ is the difference and $D$ the count, the reverse
of item A. I keep the source's letters so the names below match the files. Let
$K = (N_{00} N_{01} N_{10} N_{11} D_{g_1} D_{g_2} D_{g_3} D_{g_4} D_{g_5})^2$
(\code{g12345\_COMMON\_Z}, kernel/foundation/VMStep.v). The kernel computes the 21 integers
$K H_{ij}$ (\code{cleared\_g12345\_H11\_Z} to \code{cleared\_g12345\_H56\_Z}), the 15
integers of $S^{(6)}$ at scale $K^2$ and the 10 integers of $S^{(5)}$ at scale $K^4$, each by
\code{schur\_step\_Z}, $h_{11} h_{ij} - h_{1i} h_{1j}$ on integers. The
decider \code{q1ab\_g12345\_check\_z\_kernel} is the conjunction of: $N_{xy} > 0$ for the four
pairs; $D_{g_k} > 0$ for $k = 1..5$; $-D_{g_k} < N_{g_k} < D_{g_k}$ for $k = 1..5$; and six
strict positivities, namely $K H_{11} > 0$, $K^2 S^{(6)}_{22} > 0$, and the four leading
minors of the integer $S^{(5)}$. The instruction's check
\code{q1ab\_g12345\_full\_integer\_check\_kernel} is \code{column\_contractive\_check\_witness} of item
E and this decider.
\end{definition}

The bridge lemmas, for example \code{cleared\_g12345\_H11\_Z\_bridge}
(QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v), prove that each cleared integer, read as a real, equals the
corresponding real quantity times the stated positive power of $K$. A $k \times k$ leading
minor of a matrix scaled by $c > 0$ scales by $c^k$. So every integer positivity holds exactly
when the real one does.

\begin{theorem}[Full 1+AB check, no trap implies PSD]\label{thm:chsh-g12345}
\code{chsh\_lassert\_1ab\_g12345\_no\_trap\_implies\_npa\_psd\_q1ab}
(kernel/quantum/QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v). Let $s$ be a state with error flag false and
let $s'$ result from \code{instr\_chsh\_lassert\_1ab\_g12345} with declared cost $d$ and ten bucket counts
for $\gamma_1, \ldots, \gamma_5$. If the program counter of $s'$ is that of $s$ plus one and
the error flag is unchanged, then the matrix of Definition~\ref{def:chsh-nine} at the four state
correlators and $\gamma_k = N_{g_k}/D_{g_k}$ is symmetric and \code{PSD9}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
As in Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-notrap}, no trap means the check passed. The bucket conjuncts make every
denominator positive, the bridges carry the six integer positivities to the real cascade, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:chsh-schur-step} twice plus Lemma~\ref{lem:chsh-sylvester} give $R \ge 0$, hence \code{PSD9} by
Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-nine-iff}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Interior only]\label{rem:chsh-interior}
Every test in the cascade is strict, so a passing check certifies that $H$ is positive
definite, not merely semidefinite. A point where $H$ is PSD but singular cannot pass, and
neither can a moment with $|\gamma_k| = 1$. For example, the tally of item E with correlators
$(3/5, 4/5, 4/5, -3/5)$ has $H_{11} = 1 - 9/25 - 16/25 = 0$, so the full 1+AB check traps on it
for every choice of $\gamma$, though the level-1 check of item E accepts it. The source proves
soundness only; no converse is stated.
\end{remark}

A worked example of the cascade, in exact rational arithmetic (argued here, not a Coq
Example). Take the correlators $(0.6, 0.6, 0.6, -0.6)$ and
$\gamma = (0, 0, 0, 0, -1/2)$; as buckets, $\gamma_1$ to $\gamma_4$ are $(1,1)$, giving
$0/2$, and $\gamma_5$ is $(1,3)$, giving $-2/4$, both inside the strict bounds. Then
$H_{11} = H_{22} = 7/25$, $H_{12} = 0$, and every entry $H_{1j}$, $H_{2j}$ with $j \ge 3$ is
zero. So $S^{(6)}_{22} = (7/25)^2 = 49/625$, and $S^{(5)}$ is a positive multiple of the lower
right block of $H$:
\[
S^{(5)} = \frac{343}{781250}
\begin{pmatrix}
32 & -18 & -18 & -7 \\
-18 & 32 & 7 & 18 \\
-18 & 7 & 32 & 18 \\
-7 & 18 & 18 & 32
\end{pmatrix},
\]
where $50 H_{33} = 32$, $50 H_{34} = 50 H_{35} = -18$, $50 H_{36} = 50(-1/2 + 0.36) = -7$,
$50 H_{45} = 50(1/2 - 0.36) = 7$, and $50 H_{46} = 50 H_{56} = 18$. The leading minors of the
integer matrix are $32$, $700$, $15000$ and $140625$, all positive. With
$H_{11} = 7/25 > 0$ and $S^{(6)}_{22} > 0$, all six tests pass, and with item E's $A = B = 175$,
$C = 0$ the instruction would not trap. At $\gamma_5 = 0$ instead, the same block becomes
$I_4 - \mathbf e \mathbf e^{\mathsf T}$ with $\mathbf e = (0.6, 0.6, 0.6, -0.6)$, whose third
leading minor is negative ($\tfrac{1}{25^3}$ times $-1250$), and the check traps.

That last fact is general. The instruction \code{instr\_chsh\_lassert\_1ab}
(kernel/foundation/VMStep.v) takes no $\gamma$ buckets; its check
\code{column\_contractive\_check\_q1ab\_kernel} is the level-1 check together with
\code{sum\_E\_sq\_check\_witness}, the integer form of
$E_{00}^2 + E_{01}^2 + E_{10}^2 + E_{11}^2 \le 1$ with denominators cleared by
$(N_{00} N_{01} N_{10} N_{11})^2$.

\begin{theorem}[The zero-moment check sits inside the classical bound]\label{thm:chsh-gzero}
If \code{column\_contractive\_check\_q1ab} $w$ = \code{true} (QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v, the same
function), then the four correlators of $w$ satisfy
$E_{00}^2 + E_{01}^2 + E_{10}^2 + E_{11}^2 \le 1$
(\code{q1ab\_check\_at\_gzero\_forces\_unit\_ball}) and $|S| \le 2$
(\code{q1ab\_check\_at\_gzero\_implies\_classical\_bound}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
At $\gamma = 0$ the residual splits into the level-1 form in $(v_{B_0}, v_{B_1})$ and
$|\mathbf v|^2 - \langle \mathbf e, \mathbf v \rangle^2$ in
$\mathbf v = (v_{00}, v_{01}, v_{10}, v_{11})$, where
$\mathbf e = (E_{00}, E_{01}, E_{10}, E_{11})$ (\code{q1ab\_residual\_g\_zero\_decomp}). The
check gives column contractivity at $\gamma = 0$
(\code{column\_contractive\_check\_q1ab\_sound\_at\_g\_zero}). Test at $v_{B_0} = v_{B_1} = 0$ and
$\mathbf v = \mathbf e$: with $r = |\mathbf e|^2 \ge 0$, the residual is $r - r^2 \ge 0$, so
$r \le 1$. Then Lemma~\ref{lem:chsh-sos} gives $S^2 \le 4 r \le 4$.
\end{proof}

So the zero-moment instruction certifies a strict part of the classical region: no point
above $|S| = 2$, and none of the sixteen deterministic points either, since each has
$|\mathbf e|^2 = 4$. A point above 2 needs supplied moments.
\code{q1ab\_certifies\_a\_superclassical\_chsh\_point} (QuantumPartitionPSD\_\allowbreak{}1AB.v) proves \code{PSD9}
at correlators $(3/5, 3/5, 3/5, -3/5)$, $\gamma = (0,0,0,0,-1/2)$, with $S = 12/5$, through
the $\gamma_5$ slice: its real condition \code{q1ab\_g5\_caller\_witness} asks $-1 < \gamma_5 <
1$ and
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(1 - \gamma_5)\bigl[(E_{00} + E_{11})^2 + (E_{01} - E_{10})^2\bigr] \\
&\quad + (1 + \gamma_5)\bigl[(E_{00} - E_{11})^2 + (E_{01} + E_{10})^2\bigr]
\le 2(1 - \gamma_5^2).
\end{aligned}
\]
At this point the left side is $\tfrac32 \cdot 0 + \tfrac12 \cdot (\tfrac{36}{25} +
\tfrac{36}{25}) = \tfrac{36}{25} = 1.44$ and the right side is $2 \cdot \tfrac34 = 1.5$. The
integer version, \code{q1ab\_g5\_kernel\_check\_accepts\_superclassical}, runs the check of
\code{instr\_chsh\_lassert\_1ab\_g5} on the counters $(4,1), (4,1), (4,1), (1,4)$ and the bucket
$(1,3)$ and returns \code{true} by computation.

Each of the four 1+AB checks (VMStep.v) contains
\code{column\_contractive\_check\_witness} as a conjunct, so a passing 1+AB check also passes the
level-1 check and inherits $S^2 \le 8$ from item E. That is a composition I did by reading
the definitions; the source has no single theorem stating it. The hardware theorems of item E
cover \code{CHSH\_LASSERT} only.

\subsection{G. The elliptope completion}
\label{sub:chsh-elliptope}

\begin{definition}[Completion and membership]\label{def:chsh-elliptope}
\code{completed\_npa} (kernel/quantum/ElliptopeCompletion.v) is the record of item D with the
within-party entries set to free reals: $x$ in the $(A_0, A_1)$ cells and $y$ in the
$(B_0, B_1)$ cells, marginals still zero. The correlators are elliptope realizable
(\code{elliptope\_realizable}) when some $x, y$ make the completed matrix symmetric and PSD.
\end{definition}

\[
M(E; x, y) \;=\;
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 1 & x & E_{00} & E_{01} \\
0 & x & 1 & E_{10} & E_{11} \\
0 & E_{00} & E_{10} & 1 & y \\
0 & E_{01} & E_{11} & y & 1
\end{pmatrix}
\]

Its quadratic form at $v = (v_0, \ldots, v_4)$ is
$\sum_k v_k^2 + 2x v_1 v_2 + 2y v_3 v_4 + 2E_{00} v_1 v_3 + 2E_{01} v_1 v_4 + 2E_{10} v_2 v_3
+ 2E_{11} v_2 v_4$ (\code{completed\_quad\_expand}). The pinned matrix is the case $x = y = 0$,
so PSD of $M(E)$ implies membership: \code{zero\_marginal\_implies\_elliptope}.

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic plans are inside, \code{deterministic\_strategy\_elliptope}]\label{thm:chsh-ell-det}
(ElliptopeCompletion.v) If $a_0^2 = a_1^2 = b_0^2 = b_1^2 = 1$, then
$(a_0 b_0, a_0 b_1, a_1 b_0, a_1 b_1)$ is elliptope realizable, with $x = a_0 a_1$ and
$y = b_0 b_1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
With these entries the form equals
$v_0^2 + (a_0 v_1 + a_1 v_2 + b_0 v_3 + b_1 v_4)^2$. Expanding the second square gives
$a_0^2 v_1^2 + \cdots$ on the diagonal, which is $v_1^2 + \cdots$ by the unit squares, and the
cross terms $2 a_0 a_1 v_1 v_2 = 2x v_1 v_2$, $2 a_0 b_0 v_1 v_3 = 2E_{00} v_1 v_3$, and so on
for all six pairs. A sum of two squares is never negative.
\end{proof}

The all-ones plan is the instance \code{classical\_tightness\_witness\_elliptope}, and the
classical mixture $(1, 0, 1, 0)$ is \code{turing\_point\_elliptope}, at $x = 1$, $y = 0$, with
form $v_0^2 + (v_1 + v_2 + v_3)^2 + v_4^2$.

\begin{theorem}[Convexity and finite mixtures]\label{thm:chsh-ell-convex}
For $0 \le \lambda \le 1$, if $E$ and $F$ are elliptope realizable, so is
$\lambda E + (1 - \lambda) F$ (\code{elliptope\_convex}, ElliptopeCompletion.v). For finitely
many members with nonnegative weights summing to at most 1, the weighted sum is realizable
(\code{elliptope\_finite\_mixture}). Every finite mixture of deterministic plans is realizable
(\code{lhv\_mixture\_elliptope}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The form is affine in $(E, x, y)$ for each fixed $v$. Take the completion
$(\lambda x_1 + (1-\lambda) x_2, \lambda y_1 + (1-\lambda) y_2)$; the form at the mixture is
the same mixture of two nonnegative forms. The finite version is induction on the number of
members, with the shortfall in weight absorbed by the zero point (\code{elliptope\_zero}).
The last statement combines this with Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-ell-det}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Tsirelson inside the completion set, \code{elliptope\_tsirelson}]\label{thm:chsh-ell-tsirelson}
(ElliptopeCompletion.v) If $E$ is elliptope realizable then $S^2 \le 8$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For a symmetric PSD matrix the bilinear form obeys Cauchy-Schwarz,
$\mathcal B(u, w)^2 \le \mathcal Q(u)\, \mathcal Q(w)$ (\code{psd\_cauchy\_schwarz}), because
$\mathcal Q(u + t w) = \mathcal Q(u) + 2t\,\mathcal B(u,w) + t^2 \mathcal Q(w) \ge 0$ for all
$t$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:chsh-discriminant} applies. Take $u_1 = e_{A_0}$ and
$w_+ = e_{B_0} + e_{B_1}$: $\mathcal B(u_1, w_+) = E_{00} + E_{01}$, $\mathcal Q(u_1) = 1$,
$\mathcal Q(w_+) = 2 + 2y$. Take $u_2 = e_{A_1}$ and $w_- = e_{B_0} - e_{B_1}$:
$\mathcal B(u_2, w_-) = E_{10} - E_{11}$, $\mathcal Q(w_-) = 2 - 2y$. So
$c_1^2 \le 2 + 2y$ and $c_2^2 \le 2 - 2y$ with $c_1 = E_{00} + E_{01}$,
$c_2 = E_{10} - E_{11}$, and both budgets are nonnegative. Then
$c_1^2 c_2^2 \le (2 + 2y)(2 - 2y) = 4 - 4y^2 \le 4$, so $c_1 c_2 \le 2$, and
$S^2 = (c_1 + c_2)^2 = c_1^2 + 2 c_1 c_2 + c_2^2 \le (2 + 2y) + 4 + (2 - 2y) = 8$.
\end{proof}

The completion can make a row of $E$ longer than 1 (the all-ones plan has rows of squared
length 2), which is why this proof does not use the row bounds of item D.

\begin{corollary}[The PR box is outside, \code{pr\_box\_not\_elliptope}]\label{cor:chsh-ell-pr}
(ElliptopeCompletion.v) $(1, 1, 1, -1)$ is not elliptope realizable, since its
$S^2 = 16 > 8$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Strictly beyond the classical bound, \code{beyond\_classical\_elliptope}]\label{thm:chsh-ell-beyond}
(ElliptopeCompletion.v) $(3/5, 3/5, 3/5, -3/5)$ is elliptope realizable and has
$S = 12/5 > 2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
At $x = y = 0$ the form equals
$v_0^2 + (v_1 + \tfrac35 v_3 + \tfrac35 v_4)^2 + (v_2 + \tfrac35 v_3 - \tfrac35 v_4)^2 +
\tfrac{7}{25} v_3^2 + \tfrac{7}{25} v_4^2$. Check: the two middle squares give
$v_3^2$ coefficient $\tfrac{9}{25} + \tfrac{9}{25} = \tfrac{18}{25}$, plus $\tfrac{7}{25}$ is
1; the $v_3 v_4$ terms are $+\tfrac{18}{25}$ and $-\tfrac{18}{25}$ and cancel; the cross
terms are $2 \cdot \tfrac35 v_1 v_3$, $2 \cdot \tfrac35 v_1 v_4$, $2 \cdot \tfrac35 v_2 v_3$
and $-2 \cdot \tfrac35 v_2 v_4$, as the entries require.
\end{proof}

By Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-fine} no finite factorizable model has $S > 2$, so this point is not a finite
mixture of plans, while Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-ell-convex} puts every such mixture inside. The completion
set therefore strictly contains the finite classical set, and the PR box lies outside it.
The source does not state that the completion set lies inside the no-signalling set.

The gate (kernel/quantum/ElliptopeGate.v) is an integer decider with a soundness proof. Its
completion entries arrive as bucket pairs, and an empty bucket is read as $0/1$ (\code{bden}),
so unlike item E it does not require every pair to be sampled.

\begin{definition}[The two branches]\label{def:chsh-gate}
\code{elliptope\_pd\_check} (ElliptopeGate.v): with the completion supplied as buckets and all
entries scaled to integers by a positive common factor $K$, the four leading minors of
the $4 \times 4$ block on $A_0, A_1, B_0, B_1$ are strictly positive. \code{elliptope\_ldl\_check}: with the completion and a rational certificate supplied (six subdiagonal entries over
a common positive denominator, four pivots $d_k \ge 0$ over another), the ten entry equations
of $M = L D L^{\mathsf T}$ hold in cross-multiplied integer arithmetic (\code{ldl\_equations}). \code{elliptope\_check\_full} is their disjunction.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Soundness of the gate, \code{elliptope\_check\_full\_sound}]\label{thm:chsh-gate-sound}
(ElliptopeGate.v) If \code{elliptope\_check\_full} returns \code{true} on a counter record, any
completion buckets and any certificate, then the four correlators of the record are
elliptope realizable. And \code{elliptope\_full\_gate\_never\_accepts\_pr\_box}: on the PR box
tally the gate returns \code{false} for every choice of the remaining arguments.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first branch reduces to Lemma~\ref{lem:chsh-sylvester} through the same fraction-free identity
(\code{elliptope\_pd\_check\_sound}). The second is a weighted sum of squares: given the ten
equations, the form is $\sum_k d_k P_k^2$ with $d_k \ge 0$ (\code{elliptope\_ldl\_check\_sound}). The PR statement is soundness followed by Corollary~\ref{cor:chsh-ell-pr}.
\end{proof}

Computed examples, each closed by \code{reflexivity}: \code{gate\_accepts\_all\_ones}, the
all-ones plan, through the second branch at $x = y = 1$; \code{gate\_accepts\_turing\_point};
\code{gate\_accepts\_beyond\_classical}, the $12/5$ point, through the first branch at
$x = y = 0$; \code{gate\_accepts\_pythagorean\_boundary}, the point $(3/5, 4/5, 4/5, -3/5)$,
through the second branch with pivots $(1, 1, 0, 0)$.

The gate is not an instruction. Neither VMStep.v nor VMState.v mentions it, and the file's
own header says that binding it into the step relation, a cost rule and a hardware mirror is
not done.

\subsection{H. What is not proved}
\label{sub:chsh-not-proved}

The following are cited results or open, and none of them is a Coq theorem in this
development.

The arcsine boundary. For two settings and two outcomes per side, the correlators reachable
by quantum measurements are characterized by $|\arcsin E_{00} + \arcsin E_{01} + \arcsin
E_{10} - \arcsin E_{11}| \le \pi$ and its sign variants (Tsirelson, Landau 1988, Masanes
2003). No arcsine appears in any Coq statement; the only mentions are comments in
ElliptopeGate.v. The claim that $(3/5, 4/5, 4/5, -3/5)$ lies on that boundary is such a
comment: $\arcsin \tfrac35 + \arcsin \tfrac45 = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$ by the 3-4-5 triangle, so the
sum is $\pi$. It is correct arithmetic about a cited characterization.

Equality with the quantum set. That the completion set of item G is exactly the set of
quantum correlators is Tsirelson's representation theorem, cited in the header of
ElliptopeCompletion.v and not proved. That PSD of any of these matrices is necessary for
quantum behaviour is the NPA reading, also cited.

Achievability. No state and no pair of measurements is constructed. Theorem~\ref{thm:chsh-tight} is a
point of $\mathbb{R}^4$, not an experiment.

Completeness of the checks. Every check here is proved sound, never complete. The 1+AB
cascade is strict and misses boundary points. The comment in ElliptopeGate.v that the second
branch accepts every point with a rational PSD completion is a mathematical remark about
$LDL^{\mathsf T}$ factorizations, not a theorem in the file; nor is there a theorem that the
four 1+AB checks accept nested sets.

Finite levels. For full behaviours, marginals included, the NPA levels are relaxations.
Chaturvedi (arXiv 2607.14569, 2026) shows that no finite NPA level characterizes the complete
quantum set even in this simplest Bell scenario.

Statistics and physics. Nothing here says how many rounds make a tally informative, and
nothing says the counters came from honest play; a program chooses its own trial inputs.

\subsection{I. Prior work}
\label{sub:chsh-prior}

Tsirelson proved the bound $2\sqrt 2$ for quantum correlations in 1980 and showed that
quantum two-outcome correlators are inner products of real unit vectors. Landau (1988) and
Masanes (2003, arXiv quant-ph/0309137) gave the exact characterization for two settings and
two outcomes. Wehner (2006, arXiv quant-ph/0510076) proved Tsirelson bounds, CHSH among them,
by a semidefinite program on the $4 \times 4$ Gram matrix of those vectors. Navascués,
Pironio and Acín (2007, arXiv quant-ph/0607119; 2008, arXiv 0803.4290) built the hierarchy of
moment-matrix tests; their 2008 paper applies a Schur complement to this level-1 matrix,
recovers the arcsine condition, and discusses the 1+AB level. Formal proofs of Tsirelson's
bound already exist, by Echenim and Mhalla in Isabelle/HOL (arXiv 2306.12535) and in Lean's
mathlib (tsirelson\_\allowbreak{}inequality in Mathlib.Algebra.Star.CHSH), and exact rational
sum-of-squares certificates go back at least to Peyrl and Parrilo (2008). So the
moment-matrix route to $2\sqrt 2$ is standard. What is specific here is narrower: an integer
certificate computed from outcome counters and checked inside one instruction, a mechanized
chain from ``the instruction did not trap'' to PSD of the pinned matrix and on to $S^2 \le 8$,
and a hardware circuit proved equal to that integer check for every choice of 32-bit
counters. I did not find that chain elsewhere, and I make no claim beyond it.

%===========================================================================
\section{Hardware retirement: the assumptions in full}
\label{sec:hardware-contracts}
%===========================================================================

The word \emph{admitted} in Section~\ref{sec:chip} names a set of inputs on which the
retirement theorem applies. It is not permission to hide the inputs. This appendix
spells out that set. All the conditions here are conditions on the state before the
instruction starts. A bound in one row is not automatically a hypothesis of another.

\subsection{Common notation and conditions}

Write $W=2^{32}$. A hardware word denotes its unsigned value from $0$ to $W-1$;
word addition and subtraction wrap modulo $W$. All inequalities below concern the
unsigned values as natural numbers, before any wrap. Write $r_j$ for register $j$,
$H$ for the heap base, $q$ for the program counter, and $c$ for the declared cost
decoded from the instruction. Register indices are four bits, module indices six,
and data-memory addresses seven. Thus taking an address means reducing it modulo
$128$. The stack pointer is register $15$.

Every case requires the fetched word to encode the indicated instruction and its
operands, the alarm to be down, the machine to be live, and $q+1<W$. Here \emph{live}
means not halted, error false, and the logic, game-check and coupling state machines
all idle. The alarm tests whether the ledger is below the sum of the tensor entries.
The ledger requirement is $\mu+\Delta<W$, with $\Delta$ given in each row. Even a
jump or a halting instruction has the printed $q+1<W$ premise: these are the
sufficient conditions of the theorem, not a claim that each one is necessary.

For a module $m$, write $b_m$ and $s_m$ for its stored base and size. An address $x$
is \emph{in the active range} when $b_m\le x<b_m+s_m$ for the active module $m$.
The \emph{trap agreement} condition says that the board's trap-vector word equals the
fixed LASSERT trap address in Section~\ref{sec:isa}. The partition-operation and
MDL-operation counters are diagnostic fields; call them $P$ and $D$.

For the arrow tables, let $N_M,N_D,N_P$ be the next allocation indices for arrows,
coupling descriptors and coupling pairs. A descriptor records a base and count in
the pair table, together with a label length and label word. Each table also marks
which entries are valid. The following abbreviations state complete predicates:

\begingroup\small
\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.482\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.482\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Name} & \textbf{Condition} \\
\midrule
\endhead
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
V & Every valid arrow index is less than $N_M$. \\
R & Every valid arrow refers either to descriptor $0$, or to a valid descriptor whose index is less than $N_D$. \\
Z & Descriptor $0$ is marked invalid. \\
E & Descriptor $0$ has base $0$ and count $0$. \\
B & For every valid descriptor, its base plus its count is at most $N_P$. \\
Pairs & Every pair-table index below $N_P$ is marked valid. \\
Labels & Every valid descriptor has label length $L$ with $1\le L\le32$ and label word less than $2^L$. \\
Disjoint & The regions of distinct modules in the snapshot graph are disjoint. \\
\end{longtable}
\endgroup

An invalid descriptor has effective label length $1$ and effective label word $1$.
An arrow's coupling list is the slice at its descriptor's base and count. For
composition, the output list is empty if both arrows are identities, the other
arrow's list if exactly one is an identity, and the relational join otherwise:
enumerate a pair $(x,z)$ for each $(x,y)$ in the first list and $(y,z)$ in the second.
Repeated pairs count as repeated entries when measuring the room required.

\subsection{Single-step cases}

Operands below mean the decoded operands used in the instruction table of
Section~\ref{sec:isa}. Ordinary and extended arrow encodings are separate admission
cases; where a row names both, its conditions apply to each encoding.

\begingroup\small
\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.482\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.482\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Instruction or family} & \textbf{Increment $\Delta$ and additional conditions} \\
\midrule
\endhead
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
ADD & $\Delta=c$; $r_{s_1}+r_{s_2}<W$. \\
SUB & $\Delta=c$; $r_{s_2}\le r_{s_1}$. \\
MUL & $\Delta=c$; $r_{s_1}r_{s_2}<W$. \\
AND, OR, XOR\_\allowbreak{}ADD, XFER, LOAD\_\allowbreak{}IMM, LUI, XOR\_\allowbreak{}LOAD, JUMP, JNEZ, XOR\_\allowbreak{}SWAP, TENSOR\_\allowbreak{}SET, TENSOR\_\allowbreak{}GET, XOR\_\allowbreak{}RANK, HALT, CHECKPOINT, WRITE\_\allowbreak{}PORT & $\Delta=c$; no additional condition. \\
SHL & $\Delta=c$; shift amount $r_{s_2}<32$ and $r_{s_1}2^{r_{s_2}}<W$. \\
SHR & $\Delta=c$; shift amount $r_{s_2}<64$. \\
MDLACC & $\Delta=c$; $D+1<W$. \\
LJOIN, CERTIFY & $\Delta=c+1$; no additional condition. \\
READ\_\allowbreak{}PORT & $\Delta=n+c+1$, with the encoded bit count $n$; the compared abstract instruction supplies value $0$. Its channel parameter is arbitrary. \\
EMIT & $\Delta=n+c+1$; the abstract payload has bit length equal to the encoded $n$, and the information-gain counter plus $n$ is less than $W$. \\
REVEAL & $\Delta=n+c+1$; the selected tensor entry plus $n$ is less than $W$. The certificate string is arbitrary. \\
PDISCOVER & $\Delta=c$; the encoding's evidence byte is zero. The abstract evidence list is arbitrary. \\
LOAD & $\Delta=c$; $r_{\rm address}\bmod128$ is in the active range. \\
STORE & $\Delta=c$; $r_{\rm address}\bmod128$ is in the active range. \\
HEAP\_\allowbreak{}LOAD, HEAP\_\allowbreak{}STORE & $\Delta=c$; $H+r_{\rm address}<W$, and $(H+r_{\rm address})\bmod128$ is in the active range. \\
CALL & $\Delta=c$; the stack pointer $p$ satisfies $p<128$ and $p+1<W$; $p\bmod128$ is in the active range. \\
RET & $\Delta=c$; $1\le p\le128$ and $(p-1)\bmod128$ is in the active range. \\
PNEW & $\Delta=c$; the normalized region's length and first element equal the encoded size and base (first element $0$ for an empty region); $P+1<W$; trap agreement. \\
PSPLIT & $\Delta=c$; the next module index is at most $64$; $P+1<W$; the selected module's $b_m+s_m<W$; trap agreement. The abstract left and right lists are arbitrary. \\
PMERGE & $\Delta=c$; $P+1<W$; the two selected module sizes sum to less than $W$; trap agreement. \\
CHSH\_\allowbreak{}TRIAL & $\Delta=c$; each of the eight outcome counters, including those not selected on this round, is strictly below $W-1$. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}DELETE, ordinary and extended & $\Delta=c$; V. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}ID, ordinary and extended & $\Delta=c$; $N_M<16$. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}ASSERT, ordinary & $\Delta=c+1$; V; the property string's character-code sum is $0$. The certificate string is arbitrary. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}ASSERT, extended & $\Delta=c+1$; V; the property string's character-code sum equals the unsigned extension word. The certificate string is arbitrary. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}GET, ordinary & $\Delta=c$; V. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}GET, extended & $\Delta=c$; V, R and Z. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}TENSOR, ordinary and extended & $\Delta=c$; Disjoint. The two abstract arrow operands are arbitrary. \\
\end{longtable}
\endgroup

The arbitrary operands are deliberate limitations of these correspondences. If a
snapshot omits an abstract field, agreement of snapshots does not recover it. In
particular, a result for an arbitrary evidence list does not show that the board
stored or checked that list. Section~\ref{sec:chip} separates snapshot agreement from
a statement about the entire kernel state.

\subsection{Memory-reading and checking cases}

The remaining seven cases are the two extended MORPH paths, the two extended
COMPOSE paths, the two LASSERT kinds, and CHSH\_\allowbreak{}LASSERT. They carry the common
conditions above and the following additional ones.

\textbf{MORPH, missing-module path.} The increment is $c$. Require $N_M<16$ and
$N_D<16$, and at least one of the selected source and target modules has size zero.
This is a fault retirement, not a successful arrow construction.

\textbf{COMPOSE, invalid-input path.} The increment is $c$. Require V and $N_M<16$,
and either one of the two arrow slots is marked invalid or the first arrow's
target differs from the second arrow's source. This too is a fault retirement.

\textbf{MORPH, pair-loading path.} The increment is $c$. Require $N_M<16$, $N_D<16$,
and both selected modules to have nonzero size. Let $a$ be the seven-bit address
decoded for the coupling buffer and let $n$ be its first memory word. Require
$N_P<16$, $n+N_P\le16$, $a+2n\le127$, and $a+1+2n<128$. The word at $a+1+2n$
must be zero. The $n$ pairs stored in the next $2n$ words must each have their first
coordinate in the source region and their second coordinate in the target region.
Thus neither a count nor an endpoint is accepted merely because the buffer fits.

\textbf{COMPOSE, pair-building path.} The increment is $c$. Require
$N_M<16$, $N_D<16$, $N_P<16$, and V, R, Z, E, B, Pairs and Labels. Both input arrow
slots must be valid and their middle module must match. Their effective label
lengths must sum to at most $32$. Finally, $N_P$ plus the length of the output
coupling list defined above must be at most $16$.

\textbf{LASSERT, unsatisfiable kind.} The increment is $8\ell+c+1$. Require trap
agreement and the formula's memory header to equal the declared length $\ell$.
This case retires through the unsupported-unsatisfiability failure described in
Section~\ref{sec:isa}; it does not establish an unsatisfiability checker.

\textbf{LASSERT, satisfiable kind.} The increment is $8\ell+c+1$. Require trap agreement,
the memory header at the formula address $a$ to equal $\ell$, and $a+3+\ell<W$.
The clause count stored at $a+2$ must be at least one and at most the number of zero
terminator words in the literal sequence. These are the conditions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:u25-lassert} and Lemma~\ref{lem:u25-scan}.

\textbf{CHSH\_\allowbreak{}LASSERT.} The increment is $c+1$. Require trap agreement. The arithmetic
check itself may pass or fail; retirement covers either result. Its complete
integer predicate and its mathematical consequence are in Appendix~\ref{sec:chsh-derivation}.

\subsection{What the catalogue establishes}

These are fifty-five admission cases, counting the separately named encodings and
fault paths. They are sufficient hypotheses for the retirement theorem. They do
not assert that a program can never leave this set, that a failed premise makes
the hardware incorrect, or that all abstract instructions have an encoding.

The proof divides the cases by what can change. For an ordinary arithmetic or
data-moving instruction, evaluate the register writes and the program-counter
and ledger updates, then use the bounds to replace word arithmetic by the
natural-number arithmetic of the specified instruction. For memory and partition
instructions, the active-range and representation conditions make their guards
and selected addresses agree. For arrow operations, the validity, descriptor and
capacity conditions make the table lookup or update represent the stated graph
operation. A fault path instead proves agreement on its specified refusal.

A multi-cycle instruction also needs an invariant through its internal firings:
the scan has processed exactly the prefix already visited, the partial arithmetic
equals the corresponding expression on the saved operands, and unrelated state
fields are unchanged. The scan and game-check arguments are given in
Section~\ref{sec:chip}. The coupling scan loads the next pair, checks its two region
memberships and advances its count; composition enumerates the finite join defined
above, with the identity cases separated. The room and address conditions keep
each write within its intended table. At completion, the accumulated list is the
specified one. This is how the per-instruction arguments enter the master case
split; a list of theorem names alone would not supply that explanation.

\subsection{Reading a snapshot as a kernel state}

Two readings occur in Section~\ref{sec:chip}. They copy the same scalar state: program
counter, ledger, error flag, logic accumulator, status, certification flag, four
control registers and eight witness counters. They turn register entries 0--15,
memory entries 0--127 and tensor entries 0--15 into lists in increasing index order.
The board's halted flag and diagnostic counters have no separate kernel-state fields.

The partition-only reading, $\mathrm{abs}_0$, reconstructs modules by visiting indices
$N-1,N-2,\ldots,0$, where $N$ is the next module index. It omits a module whose size
is zero. Each remaining module gets the interval of addresses from its base through
base plus size minus one, an empty axiom list and a zero tensor. The graph's next
module index is $N$, its arrow list is empty and its next arrow index is one.
This is the reading used in the checking-step comparison.

The full reading, $\mathrm{abs}$, uses the same modules and intervals, but gives each
module its sixteen stored tensor entries. It visits arrow indices in descending
order below $N_M$, omitting invalid slots. A valid entry supplies source, target and
identity flag. Its descriptor supplies the coupling label and the list of pairs in
its stored range, read in increasing offset order and skipping absent pairs.
An absent descriptor supplies an empty pair list and the default empty-coupling
label. Each reconstructed arrow has certification cost zero. The graph's next arrow
index is $N_M$. This is the reading in Theorem~\ref{thm:u25-driven}. The theorem compares
the reconstructed state; it does not recover evidence absent from the snapshot.

\subsection{The full-state bridge conditions}

The full-state bridge and clocked retirement have different hypotheses. The
following predicates complete the definition of $\mathrm{WF}$ in
Theorem~\ref{thm:u25-driven}. They concern the snapshot's natural-number fields and
optional table entries, before any extra bounds required by the clocked board.

A \emph{well-formed partition table} has $1\le N\le64$. A \emph{well-formed arrow table}
has no valid arrow at an index at least $N_M$. The \emph{empty-descriptor condition}
says that descriptor zero is absent. The \emph{extended invariant} consists of these
three conditions together with $N_D>0$ and all of the following: every valid arrow
names a descriptor index below $N_D$; every present descriptor's base plus count is
at most $N_P$; and every slot in every present descriptor's range holds a pair.
It does not require every index below $N_D$ to hold a descriptor.

The \emph{stack condition} is $p<128$ and $(p-1)\bmod2^{64}<128$, where $p=r_{15}$ and
the subtraction in that second expression is subtraction modulo $2^{64}$.
Since $p<128$, this is equivalent to $1\le p<128$.
A \emph{clear tensor slot} has every stored tensor entry zero, including entries beyond
the sixteen that the reading retains.

\begingroup\small
\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.482\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.482\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Instruction} & \textbf{Additional condition for $\mathrm{WF}$} \\
\midrule
\endhead
\bottomrule
\endlastfoot
CALL & Stack condition and program counter below $128$. \\
RET & Stack condition. \\
CHSH\_\allowbreak{}TRIAL & Each of its four supplied operands is $0$ or $1$. \\
LASSERT & Declared length equals the formula memory header. \\
TENSOR\_\allowbreak{}SET & Both tensor indices are below $4$. \\
TENSOR\_\allowbreak{}GET & Both tensor indices are below $4$, and the selected module exists in the reconstructed graph. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}DELETE, MORPH\_\allowbreak{}ASSERT & Well-formed arrow table. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}GET, COMPOSE, MORPH\_\allowbreak{}TENSOR & Extended invariant. \\
MORPH & Extended invariant; source and target module indices are below $N$ and each has positive size. \\
MORPH\_\allowbreak{}ID & Empty-descriptor condition; selected module index below $N$ with positive size. \\
PNEW & $N\le64$, normalized input region nonempty, and tensor slot $N$ clear. \\
PSPLIT & Well-formed partition table; selected index reduced modulo $64$ is below $N$ and has size at least $2$; sizes at $N$ and $N+1$ are zero and both tensor slots are clear. \\
PMERGE & Well-formed partition table; both indices reduced modulo $64$ are below $N$, distinct and of positive size; size at $N$ is zero and its tensor slot is clear. \\
Every other instruction & True. \\
\end{longtable}
\endgroup

These are the conditions on one step. The run theorem asks for the appropriate row
again at every fetched instruction; it does not infer their preservation from reset.

%===========================================================================
\section{Constructing the quoting operation}
\label{sec:quoting-construction}
%===========================================================================

The proof in Section~\ref{sec:diagonal} uses a program that takes the code of a term
and returns the code of that code. Here is its construction. Nothing in the operation
lets a program inspect itself by magic: its input is an ordinary tree encoded as a
closed lambda term.

\subsection{Numerals and syntax as data}

For readability, the formulas below give names to bound variables. Renaming a bound
variable changes nothing; the underlying syntax uses the de Bruijn indices of
Definition~\ref{def:u12-L}. Applications associate to the left. Write $X\Downarrow Y$
here for a finite sequence of the weak call-by-value steps ending in the value $Y$.

Scott numerals are the following closed values:
\[
\overline{0}=\lambda z.\lambda s.z,
\qquad
\overline{n+1}=\lambda z.\lambda s.s\,\overline n.
\]
Thus a numeral selects either the supplied zero case or the supplied successor case,
passing its predecessor to the latter. The cases below are values, so choosing one
does not prematurely run the other.

The three syntax constructors, operating on already encoded children, are
\[
\begin{aligned}
V&=\lambda n.\lambda v.\lambda a.\lambda l.v\,n,\\
A&=\lambda p.\lambda q.\lambda v.\lambda a.\lambda l.a\,p\,q,\\
L&=\lambda p.\lambda v.\lambda a.\lambda l.l\,p.
\end{aligned}
\]
For a variable of index $n$, an application and an abstraction, respectively, define
their codes by the following resulting values:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\ulcorner\#n\urcorner&=\lambda v.\lambda a.\lambda l.v\,\overline n,\\
\ulcorner p\,q\urcorner&=\lambda v.\lambda a.\lambda l.a\,\ulcorner p\urcorner\,\ulcorner q\urcorner,\\
\ulcorner\lambda p\urcorner&=\lambda v.\lambda a.\lambda l.l\,\ulcorner p\urcorner.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, $V\,\overline n$, $A\,\ulcorner p\urcorner\,\ulcorner q\urcorner$ and
$L\,\ulcorner p\urcorner$ reduce to these three codes. A code is closed even when
the term it describes has a free variable: the index of that variable is stored
as a numeral. It is data inside the code, not a free variable of the code.

\subsection{Recursion without running under a lambda}

The usual self-application trick has to delay its recursive call in a call-by-value
language. Use
\[
W=\lambda x.\lambda f.\lambda v.\ f\,(\lambda a.x\,x\,f\,a)\,v,
\qquad
\operatorname{rec}(F)=\lambda v.W\,W\,F\,v.
\]
When $F$ and $u$ are closed values, beta reduction gives
\[
\operatorname{rec}(F)\,u
\longrightarrow W\,W\,F\,u
\longrightarrow^{*} F\,(\lambda a.W\,W\,F\,a)\,u
=F\,(\operatorname{rec}(F))\,u.
\]
The recursive argument is a lambda, hence already a value. It starts work only when
$F$ applies it to an argument. That is the whole reason this construction survives
the call-by-value rule.

\subsection{Quoting numerals}

Let $E_j=\ulcorner\#j\urcorner$ for $j=0,1,2$, and let
$Z=\ulcorner\overline0\urcorner$, obtained directly from the finite syntax of
$\overline0=\lambda\lambda.1$. Write $L^k(X)$ for $k$ nested applications of the
syntax builder $L$ to $X$; it is an abbreviation for constructing $k$ lambda nodes,
not a new operation of the language.

Define
\[
F_N=\lambda r.\lambda n.\ n\,Z\,
       (\lambda k.L^2(A\,E_0\,(r\,k))),
\qquad Q_N=\operatorname{rec}(F_N).
\]
Then $Q_N\,\overline n\Downarrow\ulcorner\overline n\urcorner$, by induction on $n$.
At zero the Scott numeral selects $Z$. At a successor it passes $\overline n$ to
the second case; the induction hypothesis supplies the code of $\overline n$,
and the builders produce the code of $\lambda\lambda.(\#0\,\overline n)$,
which is exactly the syntax of $\overline{n+1}$.

\subsection{Quoting terms}

For a proposed recursive call $r$, define three handlers:
\[
\begin{aligned}
H_V&=\lambda n.L^3(A\,E_2\,(Q_N\,n)),\\
H_A(r)&=\lambda p.\lambda q.L^3(A\,(A\,E_1\,(r\,p))\,(r\,q)),\\
H_L(r)&=\lambda p.L^3(A\,E_0\,(r\,p)).
\end{aligned}
\]
Now set
\[
F_Q=\lambda r.\lambda t.t\,H_V\,(H_A(r))\,(H_L(r)),
\qquad Q=\operatorname{rec}(F_Q).
\]
The handlers are lambdas and so are values. The Scott code of the input chooses
one of them and hands it the encoded children. Induction on the represented term
proves $Q\,\ulcorner t\urcorner\Downarrow\ulcorner\ulcorner t\urcorner\urcorner$:

\begin{itemize}
\item For $t=\#n$, the first handler constructs three lambda nodes over an application
of variable $2$ to the quoted numeral. That is the syntax of
$\lambda\lambda\lambda.(\#2\,\overline n)$, the code of $\#n$.
\item For $t=p\,q$, the induction hypotheses quote both child codes. The second handler
constructs three lambdas over variable $1$ applied to those two codes. That is
the syntax of the application code.
\item For $t=\lambda p$, the last handler constructs three lambdas over variable $0$
applied to the quoted child code. That is the syntax of the abstraction code.
\end{itemize}

Each recursive call works on a proper child of the finite input tree, or on a
smaller numeral. Each builder takes finitely many beta steps. The induction therefore
establishes termination as well as the value returned.

The $\mathrm{mkapp}$ used in Section~\ref{sec:diagonal} is the builder $A$ here (not the
term called $A$ in that proof). With $Q$ and that builder written out, its self-referential
term has every piece on
the page. The companion names are \code{mk\_app\_enc}, \code{rec\_spec}, \code{Qn\_spec} and \code{Q\_spec}
(LRecursion.v); the construction above is the argument those names identify.

%===========================================================================
\section{The two fixed interpreters, in full}
\label{sec:fixed-interpreters}
%===========================================================================

Section~\ref{sec:interpreters} uses two fixed programs. Their code is part of the
construction, so here it is. Each listing runs on the unbounded instruction semantics
in Section~\ref{sec:isa}. Sixteen registers hold natural numbers. Subtraction stops at
zero. Left shift by $b$ multiplies by $2^b$; right shift divides by $2^b$ and discards
the remainder. AND and OR act on binary digits.

LOAD\_\allowbreak{}IMM takes a destination and a constant; XFER takes a destination and a source.
Arithmetic and bit instructions take a destination followed by two source-register
indices. JUMP takes an absolute instruction address; JNEZ takes a source-register
index and an absolute address. A taken jump replaces the program counter; otherwise
it advances by one. All listed instructions have declared cost zero, omitted from
the operands. Fetching beyond the listing ends the host run.

\subsection{Packing the program}

For words $a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1}$ choose a positive width $w$ with $a_j<2^w$ for every
$j$. Such a width exists for every finite list. Store
\[
C=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a_j2^{wj},\qquad
\operatorname{fetch}(C,w,p)=\left\lfloor C/2^{wp}\right\rfloor\bmod2^w.
\]
Fetch is a right shift followed by an AND with $2^w-1$. Repeated division by $2^w$
proves that it returns $a_p$ for $p<n$ and zero for $p\ge n$. The width condition
prevents a word spilling into its neighbour. Code and width are inputs, so the
host listing stays fixed when the guest program grows.

\subsection{The four-register guest}

The twelve-instruction guest of Definition~\ref{def:u22-guest} encodes an instruction as
\[
o+16d+64s_1+256s_2+1024c+262144v,
\]
where $o$ is the opcode, $d,s_1,s_2<4$ are register indices, $c<256$ is its declared
cost and $v$ is an immediate natural number. Unused fields are zero. These fields
occupy bits 0--3, 4--5, 6--7, 8--9, 10--17 and 18 upward.

Every genuine guest word has a nonzero opcode; zero is the end sentinel from an

has a different halt instruction.

Host registers 0--3 hold guest registers; 11 and 12 hold the guest ledger and program
counter; 13 and 14 hold width and code. Register 9 holds status: zero running, one
terminated, two malformed. Registers 4--8, 10 and 15 are scratch. Begin at host
address zero with running status. Other host fields remain unchanged. The guest

To verify one iteration, split it at its branch destinations. Addresses 0--6 fetch
the word; 7--22 select the first source register and 23--38 the second. Each two-bit
index selects one of registers 0--3. Addresses 39--40 extract the opcode. Zero takes
41--43 to address 122 with status one. Successive subtractions at 44, 47, 52, 56,
60, 64, 68, 72, 76, 80, 84 and 89 dispatch the twelve genuine opcodes. Arithmetic
results go to register 6; 99--114 writes that result to the destination. A jump
writes register 12 directly and skips its ordinary increment at 115. Addresses
116--120 extract and add the guest cost; 121 returns to address zero.

This proves the block lemma in Theorem~\ref{thm:u22-self-interpreter} by direct
evaluation: a guest step has a finite, positive host block with the same new guest
fields. No valid opcode takes the malformed exit at 97--98. The displayed branches
also rule out an exit partway through an ordinary block. Induction on completed
blocks supplies both directions of the correspondence, with a final sentinel block
for termination.

\subsection{The two-counter guest}

Word codes are $0$ for halt, $1$ for increment counter zero, $2$ for increment
counter one, $3+8t$ for decrement counter zero and jump to $t$, and $4+8t$ for the
same operation on counter one. A zero counter stays zero and falls through; a
positive counter is decremented and takes the jump. Halt has no successor.
The same packing formula applies. Fetching outside the program returns zero and
therefore halts too.

Registers 11 and 10 hold counters zero and one, register 12 the guest program
counter, and 13 and 14 width and code. Register 9 has the three status values above.
Registers 0--8 and 15 are scratch. At the canonical initial boundary the scratch
registers, status and host program counter are zero. The host ledger and all
non-register fields are preserved.

Addresses 0--8 fetch the word and extract its low three bits. Opcode zero takes
9--11 to the end with halted status. Addresses 12--17 increment counter zero;
18--24 increment counter one. Addresses 25--35 perform the first decrement:
30--31 is the zero branch, 32--35 the positive branch. Addresses 36--47 do the same
for the second counter. Each successful block returns to address zero with the
specified guest update. Width, code and non-register fields do not change.

Opcodes 5--7 reach the malformed exit at 58--59. The cleanup block 48--57 is part
of the fixed listing, but no dispatch path from address zero enters it.
Correctness at successive boundaries allows arbitrary scratch contents.

Every non-halting guest step therefore has a finite, positive host block. The halt
block ends the host run. Induction over these blocks proves simulation, and reading
a host run block by block gives the converse. The canonical encoding uses only
opcodes 0--4, so an encoded guest cannot take the malformed exit. This supplies the
construction behind the two-counter correspondence in Section~\ref{sec:interpreters}.

%===========================================================================
\section{Sources and mathematical dependencies}
\label{sec:bibliography}
%===========================================================================

These works identify the principal mathematical dependencies and the intellectual
background named in the book. The definitions, statements and worked examples remain
on its pages. A published result about thermodynamic cost, quantum correlations or
universal computation is not an additional theorem proved by this manuscript.

The guest recursion construction uses effective computability and counter-machine
simulation. Its diagonal step and cost restoration are given in
Section~\ref{sec:interpreters}; the counter and lambda references identify the
established machinery that makes its evaluator executable. The thermodynamic
references do not remove the explicit physical premise of the heat bound.
The environmental-record papers motivate Section~\ref{sec:pointer}; they do not prove
this book's pointer conjecture.
